div.head: ECf 18.1
div.ab:
Habet etiam rex aliam potestatem misericordie super captiuos, quod, ubicunque uenerit in ciuitatem uel burgum uel uillam uel etiam in
uiam, si captiuus ibi fuerit, potest eum soluere á captione.
div.note: Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 643–644 (November 2026): read from the page images and checked against the scan’s own text layer, differences settled against the page.
Liebermann’s upright (roman) letter a after “aliam” refers to his explanatory notes, the Erklärungen (printed as Gesetze III; his note on p. 627 calls it “Band II”), which are not yet added here.

note.seg: De potestate et misericordia regis überschr. Hr
headed De potestate et misericordia regis Hr

div.ab: The king also has another power of mercy over prisoners: that wherever he comes into a city or borough or vill or even on the road, if a prisoner is there, he can release him from captivity.
